ei.title: 서논술형 Practice2 (Ch5): Metaphors for History / Our Evolving View on Change
ei.subject: 올림포스 영어독해 기본1

fullPassage: We can make literal statements about the past, but without metaphors, we cannot present interpretations of historical facts. Unconsciously, we categorize the data we observe in the world and seek patterns that can be expressed as metaphors. Lakoff and Johnson explain that "We acquire a large system of primary metaphors automatically and unconsciously simply by functioning in the most ordinary of ways in the everyday world from our earliest days." In our common language and common culture, we agree on hundreds of primary metaphors such as "important is big," "happy is up," "similarity is closeness," "difficulties are burdens," "change is motion," "knowing is seeing," "causes are physical forces," and "time is motion." We then blend these primary metaphors to create conceptual metaphors. Working from our sensorimotor domains, we create mental imagery that can be used to interpret subjective experiences, like history. With technology came the idea that innovation and novelty are intrinsic components of civilization. Constant changes in technologies, society, and economics are so ingrained in our daily lives that it is hard to understand that this state of affairs wasn't the rule in the ancient days. A few hundred years ago, change was so slow that most people expected the future to be much like the past. The concept that the future would bring improvements in people's lives was never common, much less popular. All that changed when changes began to occur so often that they were not only perceptible but expected. Since the advent of technology, people expect the future to bring new things that will improve their daily lives. However, many of us now fear that the changes may come too fast, and may be too profound, for normal people to assimilate them.

det.korean: ② imagery what → imagery that: 선행사(imagery)가 있으므로 관계대명사 that/which를 써야 하고 what은 불가
det.analysis:
❌ ① primary metaphors to create: '만들기 위해'의 to부정사로 옳음
✅ ② mental imagery what → mental imagery that: 앞에 선행사 mental imagery가 있으므로 관계대명사 that(또는 which)을 써야 함. 선행사를 포함하는 what은 쓸 수 없음 ←정답
❌ ③ the idea that innovation: idea와 그 내용을 잇는 동격의 접속사 that으로 옳음
❌ ④ The concept that the future: concept의 내용을 설명하는 동격의 that으로 옳음
det.tip: 선행사 있으면 관계대명사 that/which, 선행사 없으면 what. imagery + that(O), what(X)

det.korean: ④ but expecting → but expected: 'not only A but B'에서 A(perceptible)와 B가 같은 형태여야 하므로 expected

❌ ③ expected the future to be: 'expect + 목적어 + to부정사' 구문으로 옳음
✅ ④ not only perceptible but expecting → but expected: 'not only A but B'는 A와 B가 문법적으로 대등해야 함. A가 형용사 perceptible이므로 B도 형용사(과거분사) expected가 되어야 함. expecting은 틀림 ←정답
det.tip: not only A but B = A와 B는 같은 형태(병렬). perceptible(형) ↔ expected(형)

❌ ① interpretations(해석): 역사적 사실의 해석이라는 맥락에 적절
❌ ② primary metaphors(일차적 은유): 우리가 합의하는 수백 개의 일차적 은유라는 맥락에 적절
✅ ③ tradition(전통) → novelty(새로움): 기술과 함께 온 생각은 '혁신과 새로움(innovation and novelty)'이 문명의 본질이라는 것인데, tradition은 혁신과 반대되므로 부적절 ←정답
❌ ④ improve their daily lives(일상을 개선하다): 미래가 삶을 개선할 새것을 가져온다는 맥락에 적절
det.tip: innovation(혁신)과 짝 = novelty(새로움). tradition(전통)은 반대

❌ ③ expect the future(미래를 기대하다): 기술 등장 이후 사람들이 미래를 기대한다는 맥락에 적절
❌ ④ profound(심대한): 변화가 너무 심대할 수 있다는 맥락에 적절
det.tip: 미래가 삶에 가져오는 것 = improvements(개선). declines(하락)는 반대

However, many of us now fear that the changes may come too fast, and may be too profound, for normal people to assimilate them.
questions.stem:
다음 우리말에 맞도록 빈칸에 들어갈 영어를 쓰시오. (영어로)
그들의 일상생활을 개선할 새로운 것들
[조건] (1) daily, improve, lives, new, that, their, things, will을 모두 사용할 것 (2) 8단어로 쓸 것

det.korean: new things that will improve their daily lives = 그들의 일상생활을 개선할 새로운 것들
det.analysis: 본문 'people expect the future to bring new things that will improve their daily lives'에서 발췌합니다. 핵심 명사 new things 뒤에 이를 꾸미는 주격 관계대명사절 that will improve their daily lives(그들의 일상을 개선할)를 붙입니다. 8단어: new / things / that / will / improve / their / daily / lives
det.tip: 명사(new things) + 주격 관계대명사(that) + will + 동사원형(improve). 관계사절이 앞 명사를 꾸밈

questions.wa: new things that will improve their daily lives
accept: new things that will improve their daily lives
